discovery: Electron spin qubits in semiconductor quantum dots: proposal and experimental realization of coherent control of single electron spins

nominees.name: David P. DiVincenzo
nominees.affiliation: Forschungszentrum Jülich and RWTH Aachen University, Germany

nominees.name: Lieven M. K. Vandersypen
nominees.affiliation: QuTech, Delft University of Technology, Netherlands

subfield: Experimental and theoretical quantum condensed matter / mesoscopic physics
motivation: In 1998 Loss and DiVincenzo proposed that the spin of a single electron confined in a gate-defined semiconductor quantum dot could serve as a quantum bit, with exchange coupling between neighbouring dots providing two-qubit gates. This turned the mesoscopic physics of quantum dots into a program for controllable quantum matter. Vandersypen and collaborators then realized the essential elements: single-shot spin readout, coherent single-spin rotation via electron spin resonance, and high-fidelity two-qubit gates, culminating in multi-qubit processors in isotopically purified silicon. Together these works established electron spins in solids as precisely controllable, long-lived quantum systems, opened a new field connecting nanofabrication, nuclear-spin bath physics and decoherence theory, and provided a path to quantum devices compatible with semiconductor technology. Complementing the 2025 recognition of superconducting circuits, this discovery demonstrates macroscopic-engineered yet microscopically quantum control of individual spins.
